# Implicit Core

> Implicit is the experience layer for AI agents.

Virtualize large agent environments. Materialize only the state each experience actually needs.

Canonical project: zeitcow/implicit-core. Category: AI agent experience/environment infrastructure. Apache-2.0. Current stable package: implicit-ai 1.0.1. Python 3.11+. Install: pip install implicit-ai. Import: implicit. Use an isolated environment to avoid shared import namespace conflicts.

Problem: in agent training and evaluation, the possible environment may contain far more state than an individual episode needs. An experience addresses a coordinate in a versioned environment instead of eagerly constructing the whole environment for every run.

Mechanism: a lightweight adapter plans initial state pages; ResourceSource supplies required pages on demand through PagedState, including declared dependencies. Writes are episode-local. Keep the existing agent, framework and native evaluator; real environment adapters live in the application and use the Python SDK.

Reproducibility: versioned experience identities, seed streams, source versions and resource hashes support provenance and checking state. Reproducing execution also requires immutable contents, fixed seeds, compatible pinned agents/adapters and deterministic sources and execution. External services and effects need application-owned control, capture or reconciliation.

This is logical experience/environment-state materialization. VM/container snapshots, filesystem paging and dataset streaming can complement it. It does not provide prompt compression or lazy MCP tool discovery. Measure overhead for small/already lazy state, nearly all-state access or state that cannot be cleanly partitioned.

Historical rc1: 155/155 equivalent cases, 93.88% aggregate/94.40% mean/99.55% median retained serialized/materialized-state reduction. Bytes are not RAM. See the benchmark methodology and results for measured latency tradeoffs. Restricted native replay assets are not shipped.

MCP is local stdio with eight bounded synthetic tools whose definitions are exposed normally. It demonstrates addressed state and on-demand materialization; custom adapters use SDK tests. Repository plugin source is separate from public directory acceptance. No hosted endpoint is claimed.
